title: Adi Vaani
subtitle: Bringing India’s Tribal Languages into the Digital Age
body_text: Adi Vaani is an AI-powered platform of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs that makes tribal languages more accessible through translation and digital tools. As on 15 October 2026, it supports text translation in nine tribal languages and has recorded over 35,000 Android downloads. State Tribal Research Institutes have contributed approximately 13.9 lakh text sentences and around 300 hours of speech data to train its models. The Working Group on Tribal Languages, which first met on 15 October 2026, discussed positioning Adi Vaani as the National Tribal Language Repository. By reducing language barriers, it can support mother-tongue education, healthcare communication, access to public services and cultural preservation. Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is observing Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada across the country from 1 to 15 November 2026 , culminating in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November , the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda . The Government of India designated 15 November as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in 2021 . The Pakhwada is a focused, time-bound drive to accelerate the Ministry’s flagship programmes and take their benefits to tribal families at the last mile. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, over 300 projects for tribal communities across States are being taken up, with 228 ready for inauguration and 74 for foundation stone laying . Two national digital initiatives, the Jan-HIT Portal and the National FRA Digital Platform , are also being launched. Tribal Research Institutes have planned more than 160 activities in 19 States/UTs . Click to Read More: Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026: Nationwide Celebrations to Honour Tribal Heritage, Empower Communities and Accelerate Last-Mile Delivery of Welfare Schemes A language is more than a means of communication. It carries the history, identity and knowledge of a community. Across India, tribal languages have carried folk tales, songs and valuable knowledge of forests, farming and medicine across generations. Yet many are low-resource languages , spoken by relatively small communities and passed down largely through oral traditions. With limited written records and very little digital text or speech data, these languages have remained largely unsupported by modern language technologies. Adi Vaani aims to bridge this gap by using artificial intelligence. It uses technology to document, translate and promote tribal languages , creating new opportunities for their preservation, learning and everyday use. Adi Vaani: Connecting Language with Technology Adi Vaani is an AI-powered translation and language platform built with tribal communities, for tribal communities. Launched by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs on 1 September 2025 , it was developed by a national consortium led by IIT Delhi , along with BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad, IIIT Nava Raipur and the Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) of Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Meghalaya. Over time, several other State Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) also joined the initiative, further expanding its collaborative reach across the country. Bridging the Digital Divide: Mission and Vision Adi Vaani aims to bridge the digital divide for tribal communities through AI-powered translation. Its vision is a digitally inclusive India where no citizen is left behind due to language barriers. The initiative is guided by respect, collaboration, authenticity, innovation and empowerment through digital inclusion. Expanding Language Coverage and Digital Reach Starting with Santali, Bhili, Mundari and Gondi , Adi Vaani has expanded to offer text translation in nine tribal languages as on 15 October 2026. It also provides speech translation, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), video subtitling and access to more than 300 language primers . Primers are basic language learning resources designed to help new learners understand and practise tribal languages easily. The platform has recorded over 35,000 Android downloads and around 6,500 monthly users , indicating its growing digital reach. Building AI with Tribal Communities What makes Adi Vaani different is its community-based approach . Native speakers contribute words, sentences and voice recordings through TRIs and AdiKosh. These are checked by language experts before being used to train AI models. The project aims to collect around 1,00,000 sentence pairs and 100 hours of speech recordings per language . As on 15 October 2026, State TRIs had contributed approximately 13.9 lakh text sentences across ten languages and around 300 hours of speech data. This approach combines modern technology with community knowledge to support the preservation, learning and everyday use of tribal languages. Each language passes through five phases, from data collection to integration on the platform, and the models are retrained as the community contributes more data. What Are TRIs and AdiKosh? Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) are research bodies established at the State level under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. They serve as centres of knowledge and research, functioning as think tanks for tribal development. TRIs preserve tribal cultural heritage, while providing research-based inputs to States for evidence-based planning and appropriate legislation. They build the capacity of tribal communities, as well as of individuals and institutions associated with tribal affairs. They also disseminate information and create awareness on tribal issues. AdiKosh is the word bank of Adi Vaani. It holds dictionary entries and spoken sentences, recorded by verified speakers and reviewed by the language team. Speech recorded through AdiKosh is validated by TRIs before it is used to train the models. The platform’s key features include: Text-to-text translation: Translation between supported tribal languages and languages such as Hindi and English. Speech-to-text: Converts spoken words into text, supporting oral-language documentation. Speech-to-speech translation: Translates speech by linking speech recognition, translation and speech synthesis. Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Extracts text from images and scanned documents for translation. Video subtitling: Supports translation of video content and public information into tribal languages. Digital dictionaries and primers: Provide vocabulary, meanings and basic learning resources. Tribal Languages: Preserving Knowledge and Identity According to Census 2011 , India has about 10.45 crore Scheduled Tribe people , accounting for about 8.6% of the country’s population . These communities have distinct languages and cultural traditions. Preserving these languages is important as they carry centuries of folklore, traditional knowledge and community identity. They also support early learning in the mother tongue and help pass knowledge of forests, farming, medicine and biodiversity to future generations. Making these languages digitally accessible can further reduce language barriers and improve access to education, healthcare information and public services. Adi Vaani’s Impact: Beyond Language Translation The usefulness of Adi Vaani extends to education, healthcare awareness and public communication, where language can influence how information is understood and used. Supporting Mother-Tongue Education The National Education Policy 2020 recommends the use of the home language, mother tongue or local language as the medium of instruction wherever possible, at least until Grade 5 and preferably until Grade 8 and beyond. Adi Vaani provides access to more than 300 language primers prepared by Tribal Research Institutes, along with 24 dictionaries and other learning resources. The National Education Society for Tribal Students has also highlighted the potential use of these resources across more than 525 Eklavya Model Residential Schools, serving over 1.7 lakh students . Their integration into school learning could support mother-tongue-based multilingual education and encourage students to engage with their linguistic heritage. Improving Healthcare Communication Language accessibility can play an important role in public health programmes, particularly in explaining diseases, screening procedures and preventive measures. Adi Vaani includes translated awareness resources on Sickle Cell Disease , a major health concern among several tribal communities. The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission , launched on 1 July 2023, aims to eliminate the disease as a public health problem by 2047. By 16 July 2026, more than 7.24 crore screenings had been conducted in tribal-dominated areas. Adi Vaani can complement such health initiatives by supporting awareness and communication in local languages. Economic Empowerment: Improving Access to Markets Language barriers can limit access to market information, digital services and business opportunities. Adi Vaani aims to address this gap by making online information more accessible in tribal languages. Its translation tools can support tribal entrepreneurs in understanding market information and government support programmes. India is also expanding market opportunities for tribal producers. As on 13 August 2026, 4,712 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras had been sanctioned in 28 States and UTs, covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries . These centres support tribal livelihoods through processing, packaging, branding and marketing of products. Digital market access is also growing. As on 18 March 2026, around 6,000 tribal products were available on the Tribes India e-commerce platform, and 1,339 products had been onboarded onto the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC). By reducing language barriers, Adi Vaani could complement these efforts and help tribal communities participate more easily in the digital economy. Public Services: Making Government Information Accessible Language barriers can make it difficult to understand government schemes, official documents and public services. Adi Vaani helps address this through AI-powered translation in tribal languages. The Ministry also launched Jago , its official AI conversational assistant, on 24 August 2026 , to make information on tribal welfare schemes, programmes and initiatives easier to find and understand. Together, these initiatives aim to make public information more accessible, particularly in remote tribal areas. Cultural Preservation: Keeping Tribal Traditions Alive Adi Vaani brings together technology and community knowledge to document tribal languages, folk songs, stories and oral traditions. Native speakers, elders and linguists contribute language data, which is reviewed by experts to ensure accuracy and reflect local usage. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs also provides financial assistance to 29 TRIs to preserve, document and promote tribal heritage, including languages, oral traditions and indigenous knowledge systems. By involving communities directly, Adi Vaani helps build authentic digital resources and makes tribal cultural heritage more accessible to future generations. Building a National Tribal Language Repository The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is taking steps to expand Adi Vaani beyond translation into a broader national resource for tribal languages. On 15 October 2026 , the Ministry convened the first meeting of the Working Group on Tribal Languages , chaired by Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The group includes representatives from the Central Institute of Indian Languages, IITs, universities, language organisations and experts working on endangered languages. The meeting discussed positioning Adi Vaani as the National Tribal Language Repository , bringing together corpora, primers, dictionaries and community stories. The Ministry will circulate the agenda items and prepare a roadmap for the work ahead. Proposals placed before the Working Group include: Preparing a national baseline of tribal languages and available resources. Developing digital archives and multilingual educational material. Establishing district-level community resource groups involving trained tribal youth. Strengthening cooperation among TRIs, academic institutions and language experts. Implementing a two-year action plan with quarterly reviews. Earlier, at the National Conclave on Tribal Languages and Museums in Mysuru on 24 August 2026 , an upgraded version of Adi Vaani was introduced, along with an iOS application and the addition of five languages. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs also signed an MoU with the Central Institute of Indian Languages on language documentation and corpus development. The Government of Karnataka and the Karnataka State Tribal Research Institute released Class 1 primers in Jenukuruba at the Conclave. These initiatives aim to bring existing linguistic research and community resources together within a common national framework. Towards a More Inclusive Digital India Adi Vaani has established an initial digital foundation for tribal languages through translation tools, educational resources and community-generated language data. As each language’s corpus grows, the models are retrained and translation accuracy improves. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the initiative connects the preservation of linguistic diversity with the wider goal of digital inclusion. Making tribal languages accessible through modern technologies can support both cultural continuity and participation in education and public services. The next step is to ensure that these digital resources become useful tools in the everyday lives of the communities whose languages they represent.
